error_types.label: Dropped or mishandled a negative sign
None of these

sign-error: Subtracting a negative is the same as adding its opposite.
none-of-these: Reread the expression and work through it one operation at a time.
Check each operation on its own against the rules for integers.
Redo the calculation one operation at a time, then compare the result with a rough estimate.

nodes.name: Integer operations
nodes.paraphrase: Add and subtract integers using signed-number rules.

probe_items.why: Subtracting a negative flips it to addition: -3 + 7 = 4.
Adding a positive to a negative moves it toward zero: -5 + 2 = -3.

error_types.label: Evaluated operations left to right, ignoring precedence
None of these

wrong-order: Multiplication and division come before addition and subtraction.
In 2 + 3 x 4, do the multiplication first.
none-of-these: Reread the expression and list the operations it contains.
Check each step against the order of operations for this expression.
Redo the expression from the start, following the order of operations.

nodes.name: Order of operations
nodes.paraphrase: Evaluate numeric expressions using the correct order of operations.

probe_items.why: Multiply before adding: 3 x 4 = 12, then 2 + 12 = 14.
Brackets are evaluated first: (2+3) = 5, then 5 x 4 = 20.

error_types.label: Combined fractions without a common denominator
None of these

common-denominator-error: Fractions need a common denominator before you add or subtract.
Rewrite 1/2 and 1/3 over a denominator of 6.
none-of-these: Reread the calculation and name each operation it asks for.
Check the result with a rough decimal estimate of each rational number.
Redo the calculation step by step and compare the result with that estimate.

nodes.name: Operations with rational numbers
nodes.paraphrase: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators.

probe_items.why: Rewrite over a common denominator of 6: 3/6 + 2/6 = 5/6.
Same denominator, subtract the numerators: 3 - 1 = 2, giving 2/4 = 1/2.

error_types.label: Added the exponents instead of multiplying when raising a power to a power
None of these

added-exponents-on-power: Look at what happens to the exponent when a power is raised to a power.
When you raise a power to a power, multiply the exponents.
none-of-these: Look again at which exponent rule applies here.
Check the result on a simpler case, with small exponents written out.
Redo the simplification, applying the matching exponent law one step at a time.

nodes.name: Exponent laws
nodes.paraphrase: Simplify products, quotients and powers of powers using the exponent laws.

probe_items.why: Raising a power to a power multiplies the exponents: 3 x 2 = 6.
Multiplying powers with the same base adds the exponents: 4 + 3 = 7.

error_types.label: Moved the decimal point the wrong number of places or the wrong direction
None of these

decimal-point-error: The exponent tells you how many places to move the decimal point.
3.2 x 10^4 means move the decimal 4 places right.
none-of-these: Look again at how the conversion between forms was done.
Estimate the size of the original quantity and compare it with the answer.
Redo the conversion from the start, then convert the answer back to check it.

nodes.name: Scientific notation
nodes.paraphrase: Convert numbers to and from scientific notation.

probe_items.why: Move the decimal point 4 places right: 3.2 becomes 32000.
Move the decimal point right until one nonzero digit remains: 4 places, so the exponent is -4.

error_types.label: Swapped the slope and the y-intercept
None of these

slope-intercept-swap: In y = mx + b, m is the slope and b is the y-intercept.
The number multiplying x is the slope.
none-of-these: Reread what is being asked about the line and its equation.
Check the answer against the graph by plotting two points from the equation.
Redo the work from the equation, then confirm the answer with a point on the line.

nodes.name: Linear relations
nodes.paraphrase: Identify the slope and y-intercept of a linear relation.

probe_items.why: The coefficient of x is the slope: 3.
The constant term is the y-intercept: 7.

error_types.label: Mishandled a sign when isolating the variable
None of these

sign-flip-error: Do the same operation to both sides of the equation.
2x + 3 = 11 becomes 2x = 8 after subtracting 3 from both sides.
none-of-these: Reread the equation from the start before changing anything.
Check the answer by substituting it into the original equation.
Solve the equation again from the start, one step at a time.

nodes.name: Solving linear equations
nodes.paraphrase: Solve a linear equation for the unknown by isolating the variable.

probe_items.why: Subtract 3 then divide by 2: 2x = 8, so x = 4.
Add 6 then divide by 3: 3x = 6, so x = 2.

error_types.label: Substituted or eliminated incorrectly, mixing up the two equations
None of these

substitution-error: Add or subtract the two equations to eliminate one variable.
x + y = 10 and x - y = 2 add to 2x = 12.
none-of-these: Reread both equations and what the system asks for.
Check the answer by putting both values into each original equation.
Solve the system again from the start, one step at a time.

nodes.name: Solving systems of linear equations
nodes.paraphrase: Solve a system of two linear equations by substitution or elimination.

probe_items.why: Adding the two equations eliminates y: 2x = 12, so x = 6.
Subtracting the two equations eliminates x: 2y = 8, so y = 4.

error_types.label: Combined terms that are not alike, or mis-added the coefficients
None of these

unlike-terms-combined: Only terms with the same variable and exponent can be combined.
3x and 5x are like terms, so add their coefficients.
none-of-these: Reread the original expression before simplifying it again.
Check the answer by putting a small number in for x in both expressions.
Redo the simplification one step at a time, then repeat that check.

nodes.name: Simplifying algebraic expressions
nodes.paraphrase: Combine like terms to simplify an algebraic expression.

probe_items.why: Add the coefficients of the like terms: 3 + 5 = 8.
Subtract the coefficients: 4 - 1 = 3.

error_types.label: Combined the wrong pair of like terms across the two polynomials
None of these

like-terms-miscombined: Group terms with the same variable and exponent before combining.
3x^2 and x^2 are like terms; 2x and 5x are like terms.
3x^2 + x^2 gives a coefficient of 4 for x^2.
none-of-these: Reread which operation, addition or subtraction, is being asked for.
Check the answer by putting a small value for x into both the original polynomials and the result.
Redo the addition or subtraction one step at a time, then repeat that check.

nodes.name: Adding and subtracting polynomials
nodes.paraphrase: Add and subtract polynomials by combining like terms.

probe_items.why: Add the x^2 coefficients: 3 + 1 = 4.
Subtract the x^2 coefficients: 5 - 2 = 3.

error_types.label: Chose factor signs that do not multiply to the constant term
None of these

sign-error-in-factors: The two factor constants must multiply to give the trinomial's constant term.
For x^2+5x+6, find two numbers that multiply to 6 and add to 5.
2 and 3 multiply to 6 and add to 5.
none-of-these: Reread the trinomial and what form the factored answer takes.
Check the factored form by expanding it back into a trinomial.
Redo the factoring from the start, then expand again to confirm the result.

nodes.name: Factoring quadratic trinomials
nodes.paraphrase: Factor a quadratic trinomial into two binomials.

probe_items.why: a and b multiply to the constant term: 2 x 3 = 6.
a and b add to the coefficient of x (with sign): 3 + 4 = 7.

error_types.label: Dropped a sign when reporting a root
None of these

quadratic-formula-sign-error: Factor the quadratic, then set each factor to zero.
The roots are x = 2 and x = 3, both positive.
none-of-these: Look again at how the equation was solved.
Check each solution by substituting it into the original equation.
Redo the solving process from the original equation, one step at a time.

nodes.name: Solving quadratic equations
nodes.paraphrase: Solve a quadratic equation using factoring or the quadratic formula.

probe_items.why: Factoring gives (x-2)(x-3)=0, so the roots are 2 and 3; the larger is 3.
x^2 = 4 gives x = 2 or x = -2; the positive root is 2.

error_types.label: Cancelled individual terms instead of common factors
None of these

cancelled-terms-not-factors: Only common factors of the whole numerator and denominator can be cancelled.
none-of-these: Look again at how the expression was simplified.
Check the answer by putting a simple value for x into the original expression and the result.
Redo the simplification from the start, then repeat that check with a second value.

nodes.name: Simplifying rational expressions
nodes.paraphrase: Simplify a rational expression by factoring and cancelling common factors.

probe_items.why: The expression simplifies to x+3, so at x=5 it equals 8.
The expression simplifies to x-2, so at x=6 it equals 4.

error_types.label: Read the vertex coordinate with the wrong sign
None of these

vertex-sign-error: In y=a(x-h)^2+k, the vertex is (h, k).
none-of-these: Look again at the equation in vertex form before answering.
Check the vertex by putting its x-value into the equation and comparing the result.
Redo the identification of the vertex directly from the equation.

nodes.name: Quadratic functions in vertex form
nodes.paraphrase: Identify the vertex of a quadratic function written in vertex form.

probe_items.why: Vertex form y=a(x-h)^2+k has vertex (h,k); here h=3.
Vertex form y=a(x-h)^2+k has vertex (h,k); here k=-5.

error_types.label: Substituted the input incorrectly when evaluating the function
None of these

function-evaluation-error: Replace every x in the rule with the given input value.
none-of-these: Reread the function and the point where it is to be evaluated.
Work the evaluation out one operation at a time, writing each line down.
Redo the evaluation from the start, then check the result with a rough estimate.

nodes.name: Function concept and evaluation
nodes.paraphrase: Evaluate a function at a given input using function notation.

probe_items.why: Substitute x=3: 2(3)+1 = 7.

error_types.label: Reported the transformation shift in the wrong direction
None of these

shift-direction-error: y=f(x-c) shifts the graph in the direction that makes x-c=0, i.e. x=c.
y=f(x-4) has x-4=0 at x=4, a shift right.
So y=f(x-4) shifts right by 4 units.
none-of-these: Reread the transformed function and compare it with the original function.
Check the answer by picking one point on the original function and transforming it.
Redo the transformation from the start, then test a second point the same way.

nodes.name: Transformations of functions
nodes.paraphrase: Describe how a transformation shifts or reflects a function's graph.

probe_items.prompt_latex: y=f(x-4) \text{ shifts the graph right by } ?\text{ units}
probe_items.why: y=f(x-c) shifts right by c units; here c=4.

probe_items.prompt_latex: y=f(x)+3 \text{ shifts the graph up by how many units?}
probe_items.why: Adding a constant outside f shifts the graph vertically by that amount: up 3.

error_types.label: Misread the function rule when substituting the input
None of these

notation-misread: Apply the rule to the input exactly as written.
none-of-these: Look again at the function notation before evaluating it.
Check the answer by working the evaluation out one operation at a time.
Redo the evaluation from the start, then check the result with a rough estimate.

nodes.name: Function notation
nodes.paraphrase: Read and evaluate expressions written in function notation.

probe_items.why: Substitute x=4 into the rule: 3(4)-2 = 10.
Substitute x=0: 0^2+1 = 1.

error_types.label: Missed a restriction that shifts the domain boundary
None of these

domain-range-swap: A square root requires its argument to be non-negative.
For f(x)=sqrt(x-3), the argument x-3 must be at least 0.
none-of-these: Reread the function before stating its domain again.
Recheck which values would make the expression undefined.
Redo the domain from the start, then test one value inside it and one outside it.

nodes.name: Domain of a function
nodes.paraphrase: State the domain of a function given its equation.

probe_items.why: The expression under the root must be non-negative: x-3 >= 0, so x >= 3.

probe_items.prompt_latex: f(x)=\frac{1}{x-5}\text{, which value must } x \text{ exclude?}
probe_items.why: The denominator cannot be zero: x-5=0 means x=5 is excluded.

error_types.label: Treated the base as the exponent
Multiplied the base by the exponent instead of raising it to a power
None of these

base-exponent-swapped: Which number is being multiplied repeatedly?
In y = 3^x the base 3 is repeated x times.
multiplied-instead-of-power: Exponentiation is repeated multiplication of the base by itself, not base times exponent.
2^4 means 2 x 2 x 2 x 2, not 2 x 4.
none-of-these: Reread the exponential function and the value it is evaluated at.
Check the answer against a rough estimate of how fast the function grows.
Redo the evaluation from the start, writing out every step, and compare the result with that estimate.

nodes.name: Exponential functions
nodes.paraphrase: Recognise, graph and interpret functions of the form y = a times b to the x.

probe_items.why: 3 multiplied by itself twice is 9.
2 multiplied by itself 4 times is 16.

error_types.label: Combined the base and argument instead of finding the exponent
None of these

log-exponent-confusion: log_b(a) asks: what exponent gives a when b is raised to it?
none-of-these: Reread the logarithm carefully before evaluating it again.
Check the answer on a simpler logarithm whose value is already clear.
Redo the evaluation from the start, then test the answer against the definition of a logarithm.

nodes.name: Logarithms
nodes.paraphrase: Convert between exponential and logarithmic form to evaluate a logarithm.

probe_items.why: 2 raised to the 3rd power is 8, so log_2(8) = 3.
10 raised to the 3rd power is 1000, so log_10(1000) = 3.
